perf.summary: Dist recomputes sqrt of integer-truncated Euclidean distances repeatedly; the same pair distances are recomputed across the DP and can be precomputed once, and Dist should be AggressiveInlined.
perf.currentCost: Dist does a double subtract, two mults, an add, a sqrt and a (long) truncation. It is called inside the i,j,k DP (the k-loop at lines 30-37 calls Dist(k->i) for every k each time j==i-1, i.e. O(n^2) sqrt total) and again at line 43. sqrt is ~15-40 cycles and dominates.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute a lower-triangular (or full) distance matrix 'long* d = ...; d[a*n+b]=Dist(...)' once at the start of Run (O(n^2) sqrts), then index d[k*n+i], d[(i-1)*n+i], d[0*n+(n-1)] instead of recomputing. Also add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] to Dist (the using is already imported).
perf.rationale: The DP body re-evaluates Dist for the same coordinate pairs across iterations; caching makes each distance computed exactly once, turning O(n^2)+ sqrt calls into O(n^2) total with the DP doing pure long loads. AggressiveInlining removes call overhead and lets Burst hoist the sqrt.
perf.risk: None for correctness: distances are pure functions of coordinates. Extra O(n^2) long buffer (8 bytes/pair) — acceptable given dp is already O(n^2); the caller must supply the scratch (house style passes buffers in). Truncation order is unchanged since each pair is truncated identically.

perf.summary: Dist(xs[i-1],ys[i-1],xs[i],ys[i]) at line 43 is invariant in j but recomputed for every j in the inner loop.
perf.currentCost: For each i, the else branch (j != i-1) at line 43 recomputes the same Dist(i-1, i) for every j from 0..i-2 — O(n) redundant sqrt per i, O(n^2) total redundant sqrts.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist 'long step = Dist(xs[i-1],ys[i-1],xs[i],ys[i]);' once per i (before the j loop) and use it in line 43. (Subsumed if the full distance matrix from the previous item is adopted.)
perf.rationale: Removes O(n^2) redundant sqrt evaluations from the DP — sqrt is the most expensive op in the inner loop.
perf.risk: None; the value depends only on i, not j.

perf.summary: long.MaxValue sentinel arithmetic (prev + Dist) risks overflow and forces per-cell !=MaxValue branches; row-base offsets j*n and i*n are recomputed.
perf.currentCost: Init loop fills dp with long.MaxValue; lines 41-43 add Dist to prev guarded by !=MaxValue. Indexing dp[j*n+i] and dp[i*n+j] recomputes j*n / i*n each access.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist row bases ('long* rowI = dp + i*n;') and reuse; keep the !=MaxValue guard (it prevents overflow of MaxValue+Dist, so it is load-bearing and must NOT be removed). Optionally use a named INF < MaxValue/2 sentinel to make the guard's overflow intent explicit and allow saturating compares.
perf.rationale: Removes repeated index multiplies; documents that the MaxValue guard exists to avoid signed overflow.
perf.risk: Do NOT drop the !=MaxValue checks — long.MaxValue + Dist overflows to negative and would corrupt the min. Changing the sentinel to INF<MaxValue/2 is safe only if all real distances stay below INF.
